name: t1utils
desc: Command-line tools for dealing with Type 1 fonts
why: Type 1 font tools open the door to PostScript font internals, a format most people never see inside.

brief.what_it_is: t1utils is a set of six small command-line programs for working with PostScript Type 1 fonts. The tools convert between the binary PFB and ASCII PFA formats, and disassemble a font into human-readable text that can be hand-edited and reassembled. t1unmac extracts a font from a Macintosh Type 1 file (MacBinary, AppleSingle, AppleDouble, BinHex, or raw resource fork) into PFA or PFB, and t1mac goes the other way. Input is a Type 1 font or Mac font file; output is a converted or edited font file.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes it as a revision of I. Lee Hetherington's 'beloved t1utils package', updated by Eddie Kohler. The README says the tools let you convert and reassemble Type 1 fonts and move fonts between Macintosh and other environments.
brief.how_it_works: t1disasm turns a PFA or PFB font into a raw, human-readable text form, and t1asm assembles that text back into PFA or PFB. The README says t1disasm's output is meant for 'subsequent hand editing, tweaking, hint fixing, and so forth.' t1ascii and t1binary handle the PFA/PFB container conversion in each direction.
brief.install_notes: The README says you need an ANSI C compiler such as gcc. Build with './configure' then 'make', and 'make install' installs the utilities and their man pages. './configure' takes the usual options; the most common is --prefix, which defaults to /usr/local otherwise. The homepage lists prebuilt packages for Debian (maintained by C. M. Connelly), Windows, SGI IRIX (Felix Ritter), and NetBSD (Jonathan Buller). No Homebrew-specific notes were found for t1utils; the Homebrew mention on the homepage is for the separate lcdf-typetools package.
brief.standout: t1disasm and t1asm give you a text round-trip for Type 1 fonts, so you can edit a font's internals by hand, which is rare for a format most people never open. t1unmac also works off a Mac, pulling the PostScript data out of a classic Mac font file on any Unix or Windows machine.
brief.status: Maintained, as far as the pages show. The homepage lists t1utils-1.42 with changes for versions 1.37 to 1.42 (an infinite-loop fix and security and compilation fixes). The GitHub README's copyright line covers changes through 2026. No exact release date appeared on the pages I read.
brief.caveats: The README warns that t1mac output will not work on a Macintosh by itself, because Macintoshes cannot read raw Type 1 fonts; you also need a font suitcase with bitmap fonts, which t1utils does not create. The README also says the tools should not be used to illegally copy Type 1 font programs. License is the Click LICENSE, a BSD-like license. Build requires an ANSI C compiler. The pages do not include a worked usage example, so the exact invocation syntax was not seen. The Windows and other prebuilt binaries are maintained by third parties.
quotes: Six free UNIX/Windows command-line tools for dealing with Type 1 fonts.
t1disasm translates PFBs or PFAs into a human-readable and -editable format; t1asm goes the opposite direction.
Note that these tools should not be used to illegally copy Type 1 font programs. Typeface design is an intricate art that should be rewarded.
fetch_log: https://www.lcdf.org/type/ - fetched OK; contains the Type 1 utilities section with descriptions, changelog, and download links (the GitHub link text had no URL shown, so the repo URL was taken from the README's owner)
https://github.com/kohler/t1utils - fetched OK; README read in full, including installation and license

judge.reason: Its disassembler turns opaque Type 1 fonts into editable PostScript and back, opening a rarely explored format rather than offering generic font conversion.

entry.title: t1utils
entry.tldr: Six small tools that take a PostScript Type 1 font apart into editable text and put it back together, plus Mac font extraction.
entry.deeper_look:
t1utils is a set of command-line programs for PostScript Type 1 fonts, an old outline font format that most people only ever see as a file in a font folder. `t1disasm` turns a font into a human-readable text form, and `t1asm` assembles that text back into a working font. The README says the disassembled output is meant for "subsequent hand editing, tweaking, hint fixing, and so forth."

The other tools handle containers. `t1ascii` and `t1binary` convert between the ASCII (PFA) and binary (PFB) forms of the same font. `t1unmac` pulls a Type 1 font out of classic Macintosh packaging (MacBinary, AppleSingle, AppleDouble, BinHex, or a raw resource fork) on any Unix or Windows machine, and `t1mac` goes the other direction.

The idea underneath is that a font is a program. A Type 1 font is PostScript code describing glyph outlines and hints, and a text round-trip lets you read it, change it, and rebuild it. It is a quiet way into how digital type was built before OpenType.

The package is a revision by Eddie Kohler of I. Lee Hetherington's original t1utils, which the homepage calls "beloved".

try_this.what_happens: Shows how to turn a PFA or PFB font into editable text.
Shows how to assemble that text back into a PFA or PFB font.
Shows how to extract a Type 1 font from a Macintosh font file.

entry.whats_unique: The disassemble, edit, reassemble round-trip lets you change a font's internals by hand, which is rare for a format most people never open. t1unmac also reads classic Mac font files on non-Mac systems.
entry.caveats: Type 1 is a legacy format, and t1mac output will not work on a Mac by itself because it also needs a font suitcase with bitmap fonts, which t1utils does not create.
